BING WAS CONFIRMED BROKEN FOR THE ENTIRE RESEARCH SESSION (2026-09-13), on both curl and the browser tool, in fresh tabs, across many substantially reworded queries (dropping 'best', trying 'beer garden guide Time Out', trying quoted-phrase queries). Every query matched on a single common word ('best' or 'London') and returned dictionary/Wikipedia/tourist-board filler (merriam-webster, cambridge dictionary, visitlondon.com, britannica) regardless of the rest of the query - see the four example queries tried, none of which returned a single on-topic result. Per the task instructions, every source below was instead found by navigating straight to mastheads' own nav, on-site search, or XML sitemaps and reading the live page - not by web search. Two sites (standard.co.uk, designmynight.com) also threw unrequested redirects to unrelated third-party sites (openstreetmap.org, lse.co.uk, and once bing.com itself mid-navigation) when driven with the browser tool - curl was reliable for both, the browser tool was not, for these two domains specifically. A re-run once Bing recovers may surface more, especially tier C blogs and tier D video, which lean on search far more than mastheads do.

'Beer garden' and 'pub garden' are used interchangeably by every source found, sometimes both in the same piece (CN Traveller's gallery asks 'What is the best beer garden in London?' then heads its list 'The best pub gardens in London for...'). 'Beer garden' is the more common term in titles (Time Out, DesignMyNight and one of the two Standard pieces use it exclusively) - see openVenueQuestions.

Sibling topic craft-beer-pubs.json already carries two general 'best pubs' lists (Time Out's and Secret London's) that each flag a handful of garden-relevant entries within them - e.g. Secret London's existing citation for 'The Lamb, Chiswick' already quotes 'particularly lovely garden'. Re-mining those specific entries for THIS topic is legitimate (the same move Time Out's own taproom guide made against its own 50 Best Pubs list), but they are NOT new sources - see the editorialLists notes below for exactly which URLs are already spoken for.
awardBodiesChecked: CAMRA - checked the national site (camra.org.uk) directly; no 'Garden Pub of the Year' or equivalent award is advertised at national level. craft-beer-pubs.json's collection pass already established that several London branches run a 'Cider Pub of the Year' sub-category alongside their main Pub of the Year (East London, North London, South West London and South East London branches all named one, per Tweedy Pubs' videos) - so branch-level sub-categories beyond the headline award are a real pattern for CAMRA, but no evidence of an equivalent GARDEN sub-category turned up in this pass. Not re-crawling all 13 Greater London branch sites for this draft-and-stop step (disproportionate before the topic is confirmed worth collecting) - worth a specific, targeted check of the branch sites at collection time, since they are already known-navigable from the craft-beer-pubs pass.

Great British Pub Awards (greatbritishpubawards.co.uk, run by William Reed / morningadvertiser.co.uk) - REAL AND LIVE, running for 2026, and it DOES have a genuine 'Best Pub Garden' category (confirmed via the site's own categories/testimonials page). But it is a NATIONAL award, not London-specific - trap 12 applies. The only past winner findable in this pass (2023) is The Gaggle of Geese in Buckland Newton, Dorset - not London, so not usable as-is. The site does not appear to expose a clean, dated, per-year winners archive as a plain page: guesses at /winners/, /2025-winners/, /2026-winners/, /previous-winners/ and /finalists/ all served byte-for-byte the same generic categories/testimonials page (which itself carries an internal page title of 'Great British Pub Awards 2020', despite showing 2023 testimonials - the page is stale/reused across years, not a real archive). If this topic proceeds to collection, worth one more targeted look (or asking whether Rob already knows a London winner in another year) before concluding the award never touches London - not force-counted here on the one Dorset data point.

No London-specific judged pub-garden or beer-garden award was found. Under SKILL.md's rule this sets the social-tier floor at THREE independent voices rather than two, once tiers D/E are collected - same conclusion barbecue.json reached for the same reason.

editorialLists.name: Time Out
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-13 - CONFIRMED LIVE, read in full. 'The best beer gardens in London', dated Monday 20 July 2026, by Leonie Cooper (Time Out London's Food and Drink Editor). Numbered 1-24 in Time Out's standard countdown format ('What is it?' / 'Why we love it?' / 'Time Out tip' per entry, with address and opening hours) - the same house style as the taproom guide already recorded for craft-beer-pubs, which WAS explicitly confirmed ranked. This piece's own intro text does not use an explicit 'we've ranked' claim the way the '50 Best Pubs' piece does, so treat the numbering as likely-ranked but re-confirm at collection (trap 11).
editorialLists.note: Its own intro links onward to Time Out's 'Best Historic Pubs in London' and 'Most Haunted Pubs in London' (different facets, not fetched here) and explicitly separates ROOFTOP bars into their own, different guide: 'If you want to be outside but higher up, you might like our directory of the capital's finest rooftop bars.' See openVenueQuestions - Time Out itself does not treat rooftop terraces as beer gardens. Also says 'quite a few of these boozers also feature in our 50 Best Pubs In London list' - that list is ALREADY a craft-beer-pubs source (timeout.com/london/bars-and-pubs/the-best-pubs-in-london); do not record it a second time as new, only re-mine the specific garden-flagged entries if this topic collects. Venues actually named here include several already in the craft-beer-pubs corpus for unrelated reasons (The Black Eel via Will Hawkes, The Chesham Arms via Tweedy Pubs/CAMRA) - fine to cite again here, but each needs its own fresh citation, per trap 7 - the craft-beer-pubs count cannot be reused.

editorialLists.name: DesignMyNight

Found via the site's own sitemap (designmynight.com/sitemap.xml -> sitemap-*.xml), not a guessed slug or the site's broken on-site search (both /london/search?q=... and a direct /london/bars/londons-best-beer-gardens-style slug guess 404'd).
editorialLists.note: Same masthead characterisation as the existing craft-beer-pubs.json entry: listings-led with editorial on top, weaker than a genuine masthead review. facetAxis.note: Not a style-of-drink axis like craft-beer-pubs (real-ale/craft-keg/taproom) - pub gardens split naturally by WHERE the outdoor space is and what it's for, which is what actually distinguishes the venues across Time Out's 24 and CN Traveller's 21. Provisional, drafted from these two sources only; may need adjusting once more sources are in. Rooftop is deliberately NOT included as a value - see openVenueQuestions, Time Out's own taxonomy treats rooftop bars as a separate topic from beer gardens, and no source read here described a pub's outdoor space as a rooftop.

values.label: Riverside / waterside
values.describeAs: benches or a terrace right on the Thames or a canal/river towpath, not just 'near' water

values.label: Courtyard / walled garden
values.describeAs: a smaller, enclosed yard behind or beside the pub, often walled or built up on a tight footprint

values.label: Huge / destination garden
values.describeAs: a large, multi-area garden that's the reason people go there at all - room for hundreds, often with its own outdoor bar, DJs or barbecues

Rebel Atlas and Will Hawkes's London Beer City newsletter (both already tier-C craft-beer-pubs sources) likely mention gardens in passing within their existing pieces - e.g. Rebel Atlas's existing Black Dog entry already says 'on the edge of Vauxhall Pleasure Gardens' - but re-reading either specifically for garden content has not been done.

openVenueQuestions: SCOPE CALL NEEDED: does 'pub garden' in this guide include a pub's ROOFTOP terrace? Time Out's own beer-gardens guide explicitly excludes rooftop bars into a separate list of theirs, and no other source read here called a rooftop a beer/pub garden. Recommend following Time Out's precedent (exclude rooftop-only outdoor space) but this changes which venues are even eligible, so it needs Rob's call before collection, not a silent decision.

Terminology: 'beer garden' outnumbers 'pub garden' in source titles (Time Out, DesignMyNight and one of the two Standard pieces use 'beer garden' only; CN Traveller and Standard's second piece use both interchangeably in the same piece). Doesn't affect the file/article naming, already fixed to 'pub-gardens', but may be worth knowing for the H1 and title tag.

Several venues found here already carry a craft-beer-pubs citation for an unrelated reason (The Chesham Arms, The Black Eel, Clissold Park Tavern, People's Park Tavern and others all appear in both corpora). Per trap 7, no citation count can be carried over from craft-beer-pubs - each needs a fresh citation recorded under this topic if collection goes ahead.
